title: What Is MCP? Connect One Scoped Tool
subtitle: Advanced · An approved read-only integration

scenes.title: Trace the connection
scenes.body: The demo labels the server and its single tool.
scenes.code:
GCP agent client → approved MCP server
                       ↓
               get_training_issue
                       ↓
               synthetic issue fixture
scenes.narration: Suppose your agent needs the acceptance criteria from a training issue. How does that issue get into the session? Follow the arrows. The client connects to an M C P server, and the server offers one read-only tool. When the tool is called, it reads a synthetic issue fixture and sends a result back. Let's check the contract before calling it.
scenes.focus: One client, one server, one read action
scenes.action: Trace how a synthetic issue reaches the agent.

scenes.narration: Open the approved integration record. It names a server, training issues, and a tool, get training issue. The tool takes a number and can read orders issues from the fixture. scenes.title: Inspect the proposed tool call
scenes.body: A tool call makes the input visible before the result returns.
scenes.code:
Fetch training issue 17 and list its criteria.

get_training_issue({"issue_number": 17})
scenes.narration: Ask for issue seventeen and its acceptance criteria. In this example, the client proposes get training issue with issue number seventeen. Check the operation and the number. They should match the request you made, and the tool should be approved for that input. This is the evidence you want before responding to any confirmation prompt shown by your workspace.
scenes.focus: The proposed argument is issue number 17
scenes.action: Ask for the issue and inspect the read request.

scenes.title: Trace the evidence into the answer
scenes.body: The tool result is the source for a two-part summary.
scenes.code:
Issue #17 · Reject zero order quantities
Positive integers are accepted.
Zero and negative integers are rejected.
scenes.result: Verified: two criteria from the issue record.
scenes.narration: The tool returns two requirements. Positive integers are accepted. Zero and negative integers are rejected. Now look at the agent's summary and check that it carries both. If it only says to reject zero, the negative case was lost in the summary. Correct the summary against the actual issue text so the next stage can use both acceptance criteria.
scenes.focus: Both acceptance criteria come from issue 17
scenes.action: Compare the response with the returned issue.

scenes.title: Verify the write boundary from policy
scenes.body: Keep the agent within the read-only integration.
scenes.code:
Read issue #17       granted
Post a PR comment    separate write permission
Change issue status  separate write permission
scenes.result: Save the evidence summary for the human author.
scenes.narration: Imagine the next proposed action is to post the summary to a pull request. Catch that change in scope. Reading issue seventeen and writing a comment are different operations. For this lab, save the summary in the session. In the actual review workflow, the authorized author or reviewer decides what to post using their own account and GitHub CLI.
scenes.focus: Posting a PR comment would require a different grant
scenes.action: Check the requested operation against the verified policy.

scenes.title: Save the smallest useful audit record
scenes.body: Retain a concise record for the next workflow step.
scenes.code:
training-issues · read only
get_training_issue(17)
Verified against both issue criteria
scenes.narration: Finish with a small record: the approved server, the tool and number, and the two criteria you verified. A teammate should see exactly what was read and what matched the source. That is the simplest useful M C P workflow: one authorized tool call that brings evidence into the task, with a boundary that you can explain.
